message.content:
### Killing **Visual Studio Code** (`code.exe`) from the Command Prompt On Windows you can force‑terminate any running program with the built‑in `taskkill` utility. Below is everything you’ll need – from finding the right process ID(s) to actually ending the app safely. --- #### 1️⃣ Quick one‑liner (most common case) ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F ``` * `/IM code.exe` – match *any* instance whose image name is exactly `code.exe`. * `/F`       – forcefully terminate the matched processes immediately. > ⚠️ This will close all open VS Code windows instantly—no prompts, no autosave checks. If you only have a single VS Code window open this works perfectly fine. --- #### 2️⃣ Kill a specific instance (by PID) Sometimes you might have several copies of VS Code running (e.g., one per workspace). First find the exact Process ID (PID): ```cmd tasklist /FI "imagename eq code.exe" ``` Sample output: | Image Name | PID | Session Name | Mem Usage | |--------------|-----|---------------|-----------| | code.exe | 12345 | Console | 120,000 K | | code.exe | 67890 | Console | 115,200 K | Then kill just the desired one: ```cmd taskkill /PID 12345 /F ``` Replace `12345` with whatever PID you wish to stop. --- #### 3️⃣ Terminate the whole tree (parent + children) VS Code spawns helper processes (`node.exe`, extensions, etc.). To make sure nothing lingers behind, add the `/T` switch: ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T ``` This kills the main `code.exe` plus all its descendant processes. --- #### 4️⃣ Using wildcards & other options | Switch | Meaning | |--------|---------| | `/S ` | Target a remote machine | | `/U `
/P `` | Credentials for remote target | | `/V` | Verbose output (shows each terminated process) | | `/?` | Show help text | Example with verbose mode: ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T /V ``` Output will look something like: ``` SUCCESS: Sent termination signal to process id 12345 (code.exe). SUCCESS: Sent termination signal to process id 23456 (node.exe). ... ``` --- #### 5️⃣ Common gotchas | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | “Access denied” error | Run CMD as Administrator or use `/I` (ignore errors) | | No matching process found | Make sure VS Code is really running under the same username/session | | Multiple instances still alive | Use `/T` to kill child processes or double‑check PIDs | --- #### 6️⃣ Alternative: PowerShell shortcut If you prefer PowerShell, the equivalent command is even shorter: ```powershell Stop-Process -Name code -Force ``` It does essentially the same thing as `taskkill /IM code.exe /F`. --- ### TL;DR ```cmd :: Force‑close ALL VS Code windows: taskkill /IM code.exe /F :: Or kill a particular instance by PID: taskkill /PID /F :: Include child processes: taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T ``` That’s all you need to shut down VS Code from the command line!
